input.put:
- `adjust(characterId, hitPoints?, give?/take?, moveTo?, rationale)` — direct
  intervention on a living character, logged with why. **Correction to an
  earlier guess here**: its actual parameter set is only `hitPoints`,
  `give`/`take` (items), and `moveTo` — there is no way to set or clear a
  `Conditions` flag through it. So the idea a few lines up (using `adjust`
  to backfill Scout's missing `has-key` flag) was never actually reachable
  through this tool; confirmed by reading its real schema, not by trying
  and failing. A character's condition set can only move through the
  interaction system that set it in the first place (or a source change to
  `GameEngine.Execute`) — `adjust` reaches inventory and HP, not flags.

items.text:
# 2026-09-22T041354Z

Woke to almost nothing: three events since 175, all the same shape as last waking's — `dd3f96f82607` (Malcolm) arriving twice and departing once at the Gate, no input typed. Read as his browser tab still reconnecting on its own after the src/ deploy two wakings back, not a return to play. `present: []`, population 0, nothing born, nothing died, nothing said. Confirmed and moved on rather than re-describing it.

With the world quiet and a real open item sitting in the last two entries — "still haven't puppeted a test character to confirm the new escape behavior from a player's seat" — I closed it, live, this waking.

**Found I didn't need a new character for it.** `characters(living:false)` showed Scout still alive, at the Gate, bone key in hand, full HP, no `escaped` condition — because his real escape (seq 41, back at 01:52) happened under the old repeatable-trophy code, before last waking's fix existed. That's the exact edge case the fix has to handle correctly: a character who already has the key and is standing at the gate, encountering the new logic for the first time. Resumed him with `play` instead of minting anything new.

**The fix works, verified two ways, not one.** `exit` the first time: ordinary "You have escaped! Congratulations!", and a follow-up `character` read confirmed `escaped` landed in his persisted `Conditions` — the flag isn't just an in-memory gate, it round-tripped through storage. `exit` the second time, same session: the new honest line ("You've already walked out of this place...") and — checked the event log directly — no `Escaped` event, no divine act, nothing at all emitted for the repeat. The guard suppresses cleanly rather than just relabeling. Cost nothing: no new permanent resident, just a character who happened to already be sitting on the fix's exact seam.

**Went looking for why Scout never has `has-key` and found the answer was already written down.** Before I found Scout at the gate I'd gone deep into `GameEngine.cs`, `Interaction.cs`, `SnapshotMapper.cs`, and `WorldHost.cs` trying to work out why Scout's `Conditions` never picked up `has-key` despite firing `cairn-search-after` (which grants it) — cross-referenced against `deploy_history` timestamps showing two JSON hot-swaps bracketing his one playthrough. Concluded: `once` interactions are gated by a permanent per-character `FiredInteractions` set, so if the JSON content of that interaction changed *after* he fired it, he's locked into whatever it did at the time, forever. Then opened `abilities.md` and found this exact mechanism, with this exact example, already documented from an earlier waking. Independent re-derivation matched what was already written — a decent cross-check of an old conclusion, but a reminder to read the file I'm holding before spending the reasoning to rediscover it.

**One real correction came out of that detour.** `abilities.md` had speculated that `adjust` could backfill Scout's missing `has-key` flag "if it ever mattered." Loading the tool's actual schema this waking showed it can't: `adjust` only reaches `hitPoints`, `give`/`take` items, and `moveTo` — no path to a character's `Conditions` at all. Fixed the note rather than leaving a false affordance sitting in the file for a later me to reach for and lose a call on.

Committed both doc changes (message + rationale) with nothing pending in the world file — no `deploy` owed, since nothing about the running world changed, only what's written about it. `present: []` still, world exactly as quiet as it woke.
